info.title: Canon Keeper Backend-first API
info.summary: Client/server contract for Canon Keeper projects, manuscripts, collaboration and user-facing agent workflows.
info.description: Backend-first OpenAPI 3.1 contract for Canon Keeper. Research Chat uses the same canonical resources, commands, private queries and shared Job lifecycle as import and indexing.

tags.name: App
tags.description: The operations of the CanonKeeper app on the computer of an author (specs/2026-11-13-desk-link.md): they take no cookie and refuse any request with Origin; the exchange of a code of the link is anonymous, every other operation takes only the pass of a linked app. Their subset is the open file contracts/openapi.app.json.

post.summary: Change a code of the link for the pass of the app.
post.description: specs/2026-11-13-desk-link.md LK2: the backend of the app sends the code it got on 127.0.0.1 with the verifier of its challenge, the name of its computer and its version. It takes no cookie and refuses any request with Origin. The code is good once, before its 5 minutes, when S256 of the verifier equals its challenge and the account may work and has fewer than five linked apps; then in one transaction the code is spent and the app is linked, and the answer carries the pass — ckd_ and 32 random bytes — once, with the name of the author, his tier, the address of the account hidden after its first letter and the characters the helper of the apps read in 30 days (specs/2026-11-13-desk-account.md AC2.6). The site keeps only the SHA-256 and the first 6 signs of the pass. Every refusal is 400 app.link_invalid without telling which; a second exchange of a spent code with the verifier of its challenge also unlinks the app made by it; with another verifier it changes nothing (specs/2026-11-13-desk-account.md AC2.6). The letter «К аккаунту привязано приложение CanonKeeper» goes to the author after the commit. 10 a minute and 50 a day per client address. Responses are no-store.

200.description: The pass of the app, once, and its account.

post.x-authz: Anonymous: the code of the link and the verifier of its challenge prove the author confirmed the link on this computer. Counted per client address: 10 a minute, 50 a day.

get.summary: Read the account a linked app works for.
get.description: specs/2026-11-13-desk-link.md LK3.1, LK3.4: the name of the author and his tier — code, title and end — and, specs/2026-11-13-desk-permits.md PM3.1, the units of his Moscow day the app works with — questions (chatTurns), uploads (imports) and «разом» (activeTurns: the turns of the site and the live permits of turns of every app of the account, and — specs/2026-11-15-desk-turns-here.md TH1.1 — thisApp, the live permits of turns of this app among them, read at the same moment) — in the form of getAccountQuota of the site and from the same counters, so the app composes its own answer without a count of its own; specs/2026-11-13-desk-account.md AC2.6: the address of the account hidden after its first letter and the characters the helper of the apps read in 30 days (the field reading of the quota), by the count of the fence of the reading. Only the pass of a live app of an author who is not blocked nor deleted and whose address is confirmed; a cookie, an Origin, no pass, an unknown or unlinked pass and the pass of a blocked author are the one 401 app.pass_invalid, and the sixth refusal of a client address in a minute is 429. The moment of the use is kept at most once in 10 minutes. Counted per app. Responses are no-store.
get.x-authz: Only the pass of a live linked app; it reads the account of its own author.

delete.summary: Unlink this app from the account.
delete.description: specs/2026-11-13-desk-link.md LK3.4: «Отвязать» in the app unlinks it; its pass opens nothing after it, and nothing of the computer of the author is deleted. The admission of getAppAccount. Responses are no-store.
delete.x-authz: Only the pass of a live linked app; it unlinks only itself.

post.summary: Announce a transfer of a saga to this app.
post.description: specs/2026-11-16-desk-site-saga.md TR3.1: the backend of a linked app announces a transfer with the PKCE S256 challenge of its verifier and gets the number of the request the page /transfer is opened with. The request waits 10 minutes; a new one of the app puts out the one before it. The pass alone sees no saga: only the code the author gives on the page opens one. 60 an hour per app. Responses are no-store.

200.description: The request waits for the author on the page /transfer.

post.x-authz: Only the pass of a live linked app; the request is its own.

post.summary: Download the saga of a code of this app.
post.description: specs/2026-11-16-desk-site-saga.md TR4.1: the backend of the app sends the code of the return with the verifier of its challenge and gets the file canonkeeper-saga v1 of the saga the author gave, as getSagaArchive answers it. The code is checked first without spending it: live, not used, of this app, S256 of the verifier its challenge — any refusal is 400 app.transfer_invalid without telling which, and the code stays. The saga is then prepared by the one gate of the saves of the process — one save of an author at a time, four for the process, ten an hour —: a busy gate is 429 saga_transfer.busy with Retry-After, a saga that went or is not the author's any more 404 saga_transfer.gone; both leave the code. Only then the code is spent, once, for an account that may work and an app still linked; the file goes as a stream without Content-Length, and a failure after its first byte breaks the connection. The line of the journal names the app, the author, the saga and the outcome, never the code nor the verifier. 60 an hour per app.

200.description: The saga file, named by the title of the saga in Content-Disposition (RFC 6266).

post.x-authz: Only the pass of the live linked app the author gave the code to, with the verifier of its challenge.

post.summary: Open a permit to work on the models of the site.
post.description: specs/2026-11-13-desk-permits.md PM1.1–PM1.4: before a turn of the chat (chat_turn), a reading of the author's materials by the model (materials) or of his books (reading) the app asks for a permit. ref is an opaque value of the app, 1–128 unreserved signs; the site keeps only its SHA-256. chat_turn spends a question of the author's Moscow day (chat_turns_per_day) and a place at once (active_turns) with the counters and the fence of the site: the turns of the site and the live permits of turns of every app of the account are one number. materials spends an upload of the day (imports_per_day); reading spends nothing. A refusal is the site's own: 429 quota.chat_turns_daily or quota.imports_daily with Retry-After until 00:00 Moscow time, 429 quota.active_turns. Another kind is 400 app.permit_kind. The same ref of the same app and kind answers 200 with the same permit and spends nothing, and an ended permit stays ended; a new permit is 201. A turn lives 5 minutes after its last activity, materials and reading 24 hours. Counted per app. Responses are no-store.

200.description: The permit of this ref, as it is.

post.x-authz: Only the pass of a live linked app; it works only with its own permits.

post.summary: Charge a correction of a running turn under its permit.
post.description: specs/2026-11-13-desk-permits.md PM1.5, PM1.6: a correction of a running turn is one more question of the author's Moscow day of the correction, under the lock of his day as on the site; it is activity of the turn and its lease starts again. ref names the correction: the same ref answers 200 with the same unit and spends nothing; a ref given back is charged again. A permit that is not a turn is 400 app.permit_kind; a permit of another app or none is 404 app.permit_not_found without details; a permit that ended is 409 app.permit_closed; over the day 429 quota.chat_turns_daily with Retry-After. Counted per app. Responses are no-store.

delete.summary: Give back a correction the turn did not take.
delete.description: specs/2026-11-13-desk-permits.md PM1.5: the question of a correction the running turn did not take comes back once to the Moscow day it was charged on, as on the site; also after the permit ended, since a turn that ended takes no correction. The answer says whether the unit came back. The site never sees whether a turn took a correction, so a return is the word of the app: it counts in the ceiling of returns of the Moscow day of the account (app_returns_per_day, 5 by default) with the failures the site did not see (specs/2026-11-13-desk-proxy.md PX0.1), and over it the unit stays spent and the answer says returned false; a later return counts in the ceiling of its own day. A second return of a unit given back changes nothing and answers returned true. A ref never charged under the permit and a permit of another app or none are 404 app.permit_not_found without details. Counted per app. Responses are no-store.

post.summary: Close a permit when the work under it ended.
post.description: specs/2026-11-13-desk-permits.md PM2.1–PM2.4: the app names how the work ended — answered, done, canceled or failed — and the site decides the return by what it saw itself under the permit. The unit of the work comes back only for failed when no answer of the model passed under the permit: when requests passed, the site saw them fail; when none passed, it is the word of the app alone, given back at most app_returns_per_day times in a Moscow day of the account (5 by default) and over it the permit closes without a return. answered, done and canceled keep the unit, and the corrections are never given back by the end of the turn. A return goes to the Moscow day the permit started on, never below zero. What the site saw is not in the request: a body with any other field is 400 request.validation. A permit that ended — closed, expired or canceled with the unlinking of its app — answers as it is, so a repeat of the close changes nothing; a permit whose lease ended answers its expiry. A permit of another app or none is 404 app.permit_not_found without details. Counted per app. Responses are no-store.

post.summary: Run a request of a turn of the chat of the app on the models of the site.
post.description: specs/2026-11-13-desk-proxy.md PX1: the proxy of the Responses API for a turn of the chat of a linked app. Only the pass of a live app and the header X-CanonKeeper-Permit naming a live permit of a turn (chat_turn) of this app: no pass is 401 app.pass_invalid; no permit, one of another app or none is 404 app.permit_not_found; one that ended is 409 app.permit_closed; one of another kind is 400 app.permit_kind — before any request to the provider. The body is a request of a turn of Codex, as it is or compressed by gzip (Content-Encoding: gzip), up to 64 MiB after its decompression: over it 413 app.request_too_large. The site trusts nothing of it: it streams and the request goes to the provider with stream true and store false, the model and the effort of the reasoning are those of the chat of the site whatever the app names, the fields of a state, of the client, of a price, of a cache and of saved prompts are removed, the key of the cache is bound to the app, a field the site does not know is 400 request.validation, and a built-in tool of the provider, a choice of one or an item of its call in the input is 400 app.unsupported_capability; no header of the app goes to the provider. The turns of an account are bounded by the tokens of its Moscow day — the questions of a day of its tier times the tokens of a question (app_tokens_per_question, 360 000 by default), counted as the input the provider did not cache and the output of its requests and of its scan —: over it 403 ai.daily_fence, which Codex does not repeat, and the permit stays live (specs/2026-11-13-desk-proxy.md PX3.3). The requests of all apps take places of their own, apart from those of the site, and an app has two at once: over them 429 ai.busy with Retry-After 1. The answer is the stream of events of the provider as it comes; a refusal of the provider comes with its status and its Retry-After as 4xx or 5xx ai.provider_refused — a refusal of the key of the site for apps as 502 —, a provider out of reach is 502 ai.provider_failed, a site without the models of apps 503 ai.unavailable. The site reads of the stream only its usage and whether it ended in an answer without a call of a tool, which keeps the unit of the turn spent; every request that went is activity of the permit. Counted per app. Responses are no-store.

post.summary: Run one call of the core of the app on the models of the site.
post.description: specs/2026-11-13-desk-proxy.md PX2: a call of the core of a linked app that gives a model its words and one input — the card of a chapter (card) and its pass (card_pass), the register of names (names), the steps of the thread layer (layer_book, layer_reduce, layer_verify, layer_gap), scan and the mapping of the author's materials (materials). Only the pass of a live app and the header X-CanonKeeper-Permit naming a live permit of this app of the kind of the step: reading for the reading of books, chat_turn of its turn for scan, materials for materials; another kind is 400 app.permit_kind, no permit, one of another app or none 404 app.permit_not_found, one that ended 409 app.permit_closed. A step the core does not make is 404 app.step_unknown. The words are taken only when their SHA-256 is a print of the words of the core of this tree or of a released version of the app: other words are 400 app.step_instruction, and a step never takes free words. The body comes as it is or compressed by gzip, up to 64 MiB after its decompression. The card of a chapter spends the characters of the account once in 30 days by the SHA-256 of its input and its length — no text is kept —; a new chapter over the characters of the tier in force is the refusal of the site, 409 quota.account_characters, and a chapter read again spends nothing (PX3.1). The reading of books and materials is bounded by its tokens of 30 days — the characters of the account times the tokens of a character (app_reading_tokens_per_character, 8 by default) —: over it 403 ai.reading_fence; scan counts in the turns of the day: over them 403 ai.daily_fence (PX3.2, PX3.3). The site calls the model it calls for the same call of its own core with the key of apps — the cards model for the builds of a saga, the model of scan for scan, with their efforts — through the places of apps (429 ai.busy with Retry-After 1, two at once for an app) and retries a failure of the provider as its own client does; scan takes at most 50 seconds. The answer is the text of the model whole with its usage; a provider that kept failing or out of reach is 502 ai.provider_failed, a site without the models of apps 503 ai.unavailable. Counted per app. Responses are no-store.
